In [[mathematics]], the '''Young subgroups''' of the [[symmetric group]] <math>S_n</math> are special subgroups that arise in [[combinatorics]] and [[representation theory]].  When <math>S_n</math> is viewed as the [[group (mathematics)|group]] of [[permutation]]s of the set <math>\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}</math>, and if <math>\lambda = (\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_\ell)</math> is an [[integer partition]] of <math>n</math>, then the Young subgroup <math>S_\lambda</math> indexed by <math>\lambda</math> is defined by
<math display="block">S_\lambda = S_{\{1, 2, \ldots, \lambda_1\}} \times S_{\{\lambda_1 + 1, \lambda_1 + 2, \ldots, \lambda_1 + \lambda_2\}} \times \cdots \times S_{\{n - \lambda_\ell + 1, n - \lambda_\ell + 2, \ldots, n\}},</math>
where <math>S_{\{a, b, \ldots\}}</math> denotes the set of permutations of <math>\{a, b, \ldots\}</math> and <math>\times</math> denotes the [[direct product of groups]].  Abstractly, <math>S_\lambda</math> is isomorphic to the product <math>S_{\lambda_1} \times S_{\lambda_2} \times \cdots \times S_{\lambda_\ell}</math>.  Young subgroups are named for [[Alfred Young (mathematician)|Alfred Young]].<ref>{{citation|last=Sagan|first=Bruce|author-link=Bruce Sagan|title=The Symmetric Group|edition=2|publisher=Springer-Verlag|year=2001|page=54}}</ref>

When <math>S_n</math> is viewed as a [[reflection group]], its Young subgroups are precisely its [[parabolic subgroup of a reflection group|parabolic subgroups]].  They may equivalently be defined as the subgroups generated by a subset of the [[adjacent transposition]]s <math>(1 \ 2), (2 \ 3), \ldots, (n - 1 \ n)</math>.<ref>{{citation |title=Combinatorics of Coxeter groups |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1TBPz5sd8m0C |last1=Björner |first1=Anders |author1-link=Anders Björner |last2=Brenti |first2=Francesco |publisher=Springer |year=2005 |isbn=978-3540-442387 |doi=10.1007/3-540-27596-7|page=41}}</ref>

In some cases, the name ''Young subgroup'' is used more generally for the product <math>S_{B_1} \times \cdots \times S_{B_\ell}</math>, where <math>\{B_1, \ldots, B_\ell\}</math> is any [[set partition]] of <math>\{1, \ldots, n\}</math> (that is, a collection of [[disjoint sets|disjoint]], nonempty subsets whose union is <math>\{1, \ldots, n\}</math>).<ref>{{citation|last = Kerber | first = A. | title = Representations of permutation groups I | series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics | doi=10.1007/BFb0067943 | mr=0325752 | volume=240| isbn=978-3-540-05693-5 | year = 1971 | publisher = Springer-Verlag | page = 17|url=https://archive.org/details/representationso0000kerb/page/16/mode/2up}}</ref>  This more general family of subgroups consists of all the [[conjugacy class|conjugates]] of those under the previous definition.<ref>{{citation|last=Jones|first=Andrew R.|title=A Combinatorial Approach to the Double Cosets of the Symmetric Group with respect to Young Subgroups|journal= European Journal of Combinatorics|year=1996|volume=17|issue=7 |pages=647–655 |doi=10.1006/eujc.1996.0056}}</ref>  These subgroups may also be characterized as the subgroups of <math>S_n</math> that are generated by a set of [[transposition (mathematics)|transpositions]].<ref>{{citation|last1=Douvropoulos|first1=Theo|last2=Lewis|first2=Joel Brewster|last3=Morales|first3=Alejandro H.|title = Hurwitz Numbers for Reflection Groups I: Generatingfunctionology|journal = Enumerative Combinatorics and Applications|doi=10.54550/ECA2022V2S3R20|year=2022|volume=2|issue=3|pages=Article #S2R20|arxiv=2112.03427}}</ref>
